name: Founders Tree

location.address: Founders Grove, Avenue of the Giants, Humboldt Redwoods State Park, Weott, California
location.neighbourhood: Founders Grove, on a paved half-mile loop trail off the Avenue of the Giants, about 5 miles south of the visitor center

access: Free (no separate fee); a paved, roughly half-mile round-trip loop trail from free parking, with a viewing platform at the tree.
transport: No public transit; reached via the Avenue of the Giants, off US-101 near Weott, Humboldt County.
verify_notes: Named for the founders of Save the Redwoods League (paleontologist John Campbell Merriam, attorney Madison Grant, and geologist Henry Fairfield Osborn, who founded the League in 1918 to buy and protect old-growth redwood groves including this one). Dedicated in a ceremony on 15 September 1931, when surveyors measured it at 364 ft and proclaimed it the world's tallest known tree; that title held until 1957, when a taller tree (Rockefeller) was found nearby in the same park. Current height given as 346 ft (105m), somewhat shorter than the 1931 claim, likely reflecting either later, more accurate measurement techniques or storm/top damage over 90 years (neither source explains the discrepancy, and it is flagged rather than resolved). Girth 40 ft (12.19m) circumference per Wikipedia; not independently corroborated by the second source, which gives no circumference figure, so the girth figure itself is single-sourced within this pass and flagged. No age estimate found in either source and none derived, since converting this girth to an age would need a published coast-redwood growth-rate basis not consulted this pass.
